title: Who Can Help Me?
title_short: Gala · Who Can Help Me? host film
headline: One question, “Who can help me?”, and the answer: for 30 years, Americans for Immigrant Justice.
story: AIJ filmed a host by the Miami River reading a full script to camera. It starts with a question people in Miami wake up with: who can help me? The answer is AIJ, for more than 30 years. The detention hotline shots from the same folder are the B-roll.

This script is not in the client’s gala script doc. Cut it as its own film. Use every line of her read. It is the client’s script, so do not cut lines yourself. Calm, warm, music-driven, and it lands on hope.
do: Open on the close “Who can help me?” take and the hook text on frame 1.
Use the full read in order. Add nothing, drop nothing.
Cover with hotline B-roll as picture only.
Match colour between CAM 1 and CAM 2.
Leave the name plate blank until Andrés sends the name.
dont: No logo, name plate or black at 0:00.
Don’t use operator voices or names. Picture only.
Don’t show any readable screen or note: C9056, C9069, C9082, C9083, C9061, C9063, C9064. C9060 (AIJ website) is fine.
No boat ad behind her (C9105 04:43–04:57 talk). Check every wide shot.
No client on screen, no detention images, no news clips.

reference.note: Picked by Sui and Andrés. Sui: the music created a lot of drama. Also from them: HBO ↗ (cinematic, artsy, not corporate) and acaciajustice.org ↗ homepage video (intimate tone). Match the pace and the music-driven feel, not the story.

rows.visual: The host, close, C9109.MP4. Bridge and towers soft behind her. Start on her face, already in thought.
rows.motion: Text on frame 1: WHO CAN HELP ME? Big, Filson Pro Heavy, white. Cut on. No logo, no name plate, no fade from black.
rows.music: Music starts under her line. Calm, warm, building.

rows.frame_alt: Host standing on the riverwalk, hands together, bridge and towers behind
rows.visual: Host, medium, C9105.MP4. Cut to the close-up C8088.MP4 (C9105 time minus 12 s) on “a mother… a child… a family”.
rows.motion: Name plate at about 00:05, lower left, 3 s: name and title still owed by Andrés. Leave it blank until it lands. Never guess.

voice.quote: Every day in Miami, someone wakes up carrying a question they never imagined they’d have to ask. A mother trying to protect her children, a child standing before an immigration judge alone, a family wondering if today will be the day they’re separated. And in that moment, everything comes down to one simple question, who can help me?

rows.frame_alt: Hands hold the AIJ brochure open on the PROGRAMS page
rows.visual: Host, then C9050–C9053 (the brochure open on “PROGRAMS”) on “providing free legal services”, then C9048 (wide office) and C9054 (AIJ banner).
rows.motion: No text. Let the picture carry it.

voice.quote: For more than 30 years, Americans for Immigrant Justice has quietly been answering that question, providing free legal services to low income immigrants, helping children, supporting survivors of violence, keeping families together, making sure no one has to face an unfamiliar legal system completely alone.

rows.music: First lift on “For more than 30 years”.

rows.frame_alt: Wide of the river and Brickell towers, host small at the right edge
rows.visual: Host walking by the river, C9106–C9108, picture only. Or the client’s Miami drone footage (Drone footage, not checked: choose on scrub).

voice.quote: For three decades, Americans for Immigrant Justice has allowed Miami to keep hope alive.

rows.frame_alt: Hotline operator with headset at her desk, AIJ logo banner behind
rows.visual: C9066 and C9100 (operators with headsets) on “a phone call”. Back to the host for “an immigration courtroom… a coloring book”: there is no courtroom or child footage. Then C9088 (very close on an operator listening) on “by listening”.

voice.quote: Some days begin with a phone call from someone inside a detention center. Others begin in an immigration courtroom, around a table where a child is learning about their rights through a coloring book … Every case is different, every story is personal, and every conversation starts the same way, by listening.
voice.src: C9105 01:19.60–01:42.75 (the transcript has “that could happen” at 01:31; the words are unclear, keep what she says)

rows.sfx: Room tone under the operator shots. Never their voices.

rows.frame_alt: Close-up of the host speaking, river behind
rows.visual: Host on the close-up C8088, then C9114–C9117 (she looks out at the river), then the skyline (C9106–C9108) on “a stronger, more connected Miami”.

voice.quote: Legal representation can change the course of someone’s future. It can help a family stay together, allow a survivor to begin again, give a child the confidence to know they aren’t facing the journey by themselves. Over the years, those individual moments have become something much bigger, a stronger, more connected Miami.

rows.frame_alt: Host in profile looking across the river toward the towers
rows.visual: Host on C9105 at 03:48. Stay on her face. Cut to C8088 (≈03:36) if a person or a boat passes behind her.

voice.quote: Behind every case is a person. Behind every person is a future still being written. And every time someone finds safety, keeps their family together, or is given the opportunity to move forward, our entire community is stronger because of it.

rows.frame_alt: Table card reading AMERICANS FOR IMMIGRANT JUSTICE
rows.visual: Host on C9105 at 05:48, then C9072 (the table card) and C9095 (logo on a polo shirt) on “every act of generosity”.

voice.quote: That’s the future Americans for Immigrant Justice works toward every day. If this story resonates with you, we invite you to be a part of it. Every act of generosity, whether it’s sharing your time, your expertise, or your support, helps ensure that more families can move forward with dignity, hope, and opportunity to build a better tomorrow.

rows.frame_alt: Host on the riverwalk speaking to camera
rows.visual: Host on C9105 at 07:41. Hold 1 s after “.org”. The crew says “Perfect” before and “Thank you” after: cut both.
rows.motion: Small text: aijustice.org, lower third, lowercase, no space.

voice.quote: Americans for Immigrant Justice. To learn more, please visit AIjustice.org.

rows.motion: Horizontal Animated logo. The logo appears here only.
